### History and Campuses
Established under a charter approved by the Illinois state legislature on January 28, 1851, Northwestern is a private, nonsectarian university with three campuses:

* **Evanston Campus:** Located on Lake Michigan in Evanston, Illinois.  
* **Chicago Campus:** Located in downtown Chicago.  
* **Doha, Qatar Campus:** Opened in 2008 in Education City, Doha, in collaboration with the Qatar Foundation.

The Evanston and Chicago campuses enroll approximately 18,000 students during the academic year.

This Handbook provides general descriptions of policies, programs, benefits, and job behavior guidelines for Northwestern staff members (executive, managerial, administrative, professional, postdoctoral fellows, technical, maintenance, clerical).

* **Labor Agreements:** Staff covered by collective bargaining agreements should consult their specific labor agreement.

document:
[SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION > 1.3 Employment Disclaimer and HR Contact Information > At-Will Employment Disclaimer]

### At-Will Employment Disclaimer
Northwestern is an **at-will employer**. Either the employee or Northwestern may end the employment relationship at-will, with or without cause or advance notice, at any time. This Handbook is **not an employment contract** or an assurance of continued employment. Policies may change without notice; current policy updates can be checked at hr.northwestern.edu/essentials/policies-procedures/staff-handbook.html.

metadata.subsection_title: 2.1 Job Application, Recruiting, and Affirmative Action

document:
[SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT > 2.1 Job Application, Recruiting, and Affirmative Action > Joining Northwestern]

### Joining Northwestern
HR and hiring supervisors collaborate on recruiting and screening candidates.

* **Job Postings:** Open staff positions must be posted for at least **5 business days** at hr.northwestern.edu/careers.  
* **Application Process:** All applicants must submit an online application through the official careers portal. Resumes/applications are accepted only for specific open positions.

metadata.subsection_title: 2.1 Job Application, Recruiting, and Affirmative Action

document:
[SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT > 2.1 Job Application, Recruiting, and Affirmative Action > Equal Opportunity & Affirmative Action]

### Equal Opportunity & Affirmative Action
Northwestern conducts searches in compliance with US, Illinois, and local laws. As a federal contractor, Northwestern actively engages in affirmative action planning, actively seeking veterans and individuals with disabilities for recruitment and retention.

metadata.subsection_title: 2.2 Accommodations, Form I-9, and Employment Types

document:
[SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT > 2.2 Accommodations, Form I-9, and Employment Types > Disability and Pregnancy Accommodations]

### Disability and Pregnancy Accommodations
* **Disabilities (ADA):** Reasonable accommodations are provided for qualified applicants/employees with disabilities to perform essential job functions or participate in hiring.  
* **Pregnancy (PWFA & Title IX):** Employees who are pregnant, recovering from childbirth, or have related medical conditions can request accommodations (e.g., extra bathroom breaks, seating, lifting limits, private lactation spaces, recovery time off).  
* **Lactation Rooms:** Details at northwestern.edu/hr/benefits/work-life/lactation-support/index.html.

metadata.subsection_title: 2.2 Accommodations, Form I-9, and Employment Types

document:
[SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT > 2.2 Accommodations, Form I-9, and Employment Types > Form I-9 Employment Eligibility]

### Form I-9 Employment Eligibility
All staff must complete **Form I-9 Employment Eligibility Verification** by the end of the **3rd business day** after their first day of work. Failure or falsification results in offer withdrawal or termination. Fingerprinting may be required for specific roles.

metadata.subsection_title: 2.2 Accommodations, Form I-9, and Employment Types

document:
[SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT > 2.2 Accommodations, Form I-9, and Employment Types > Types of Employment Classifications]

### Types of Employment Classifications
* **Full-Time Staff:** Scheduled to work at least **37.5 hours per week** (typically 37.5 or 40 hours).  
* **Part-Time Staff:** Scheduled to work fewer than 37.5 hours/week. Those working under **18.75 hours/week** are not eligible for benefits or paid time off accruals.  
* **Term Staff:** Appointed for a specific period with predetermined start and end dates (still at-will).  
* **Temporary Employees:** Casual/occasional work under **1,000 hours in a 12-month period**. Not eligible for benefits except those mandated by law.

metadata.subsection_title: 2.3 Exempt vs. Non-Exempt Status & Background Checks

document:
[SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT > 2.3 Exempt vs. Non-Exempt Status & Background Checks > Exempt vs. Non-Exempt Classification (FLSA)]

### Exempt vs. Non-Exempt Classification (FLSA)
* **Exempt Staff:** Exempt from FLSA overtime provisions (executive, administrative, professional roles requiring advanced degrees). Paid a set monthly salary regardless of hours worked; **not eligible for overtime pay**.  
* **Non-Exempt Staff:** Paid hourly. Must receive overtime pay at **1.5 times their regular hourly rate** for hours worked over **40 hours in a workweek**.

metadata.subsection_title: 2.3 Exempt vs. Non-Exempt Status & Background Checks

document:
[SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT > 2.3 Exempt vs. Non-Exempt Status & Background Checks > Background Check Requirements]

### Background Check Requirements
Mandatory pre-employment background checks are required for all regular, temporary, intern, and volunteer finalists (over 18).

* **Types of Checks:** County criminal, federal felony/misdemeanor, credit check (for financial/sensitive roles), driving record, sex offender registry, SSN check, and sanctions lists (OIG, FDA, GSA, OFAC).  
* **Ongoing Obligation to Disclose:** Employees must immediately inform their supervisor if they are convicted of a crime, added to a sex offender registry, lose required professional licenses, or are debarred from federal programs.

metadata.subsection_title: 2.4 FCRA, Drug Testing, Security Assessments, and Consequences

document:
[SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT > 2.4 FCRA, Drug Testing, Security Assessments, and Consequences > Additional Background & Security Checks]

### Additional Background & Security Checks
* **Drug & Alcohol Testing:** Required prior to employment and periodically for designated sensitive roles.  
* **Irradiator Access & Risk Assessment:** Trustworthiness assessment, fingerprinting, and federal risk evaluation required for unescorted access to cesium irradiators or select agents.  
* **Physical Examination:** Required for positions with specific occupational health and safety standards.

metadata.subsection_title: 2.4 FCRA, Drug Testing, Security Assessments, and Consequences

document:
[SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT > 2.4 FCRA, Drug Testing, Security Assessments, and Consequences > Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA) Compliance]

### Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA) Compliance
If adverse background information is used to deny employment, HR will notify the candidate, provide reporting agency contact info, and inform them of their right to obtain a copy and dispute inaccuracies.

metadata.subsection_title: 2.4 FCRA, Drug Testing, Security Assessments, and Consequences

document:
[SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT > 2.4 FCRA, Drug Testing, Security Assessments, and Consequences > Consequences of Policy Violations]

### Consequences of Policy Violations
Failure to maintain required certifications, inclusion on federal exclusion lists (OIG/GSA/OFAC/Sex Offender Registry), or criminal convictions discovered during employment may result in corrective action up to termination.

metadata.subsection_title: 2.5 Onboarding, Probationary Period, and Workplace Commitments

document:
[SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT > 2.5 Onboarding, Probationary Period, and Workplace Commitments > Onboarding & Orientation]

### Onboarding & Orientation
Features guidance, Q\&A, workshops, and checklists to help new employees integrate into Northwestern from recruitment through their first anniversary (hr.northwestern.edu/careers/new-employees).

metadata.subsection_title: 2.5 Onboarding, Probationary Period, and Workplace Commitments

document:
[SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT > 2.5 Onboarding, Probationary Period, and Workplace Commitments > Probationary Period]

### Probationary Period
* All new staff, as well as staff transferring or receiving a promotion, are subject to a **6-month probationary period**.  
* Allows supervisors to evaluate performance, skills, dependability, and conduct.  
* Successful completion does not guarantee permanent employment (at-will status remains).

metadata.subsection_title: 2.5 Onboarding, Probationary Period, and Workplace Commitments

document:
[SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT > 2.5 Onboarding, Probationary Period, and Workplace Commitments > Compliance Commitments & Policies]

### Compliance Commitments & Policies
* **Mandated Reporter:** All staff members are mandated reporters under Illinois law for suspected child abuse/neglect.  
* **Employment Policies:** Staff must comply with policies regarding Employment of Relatives, Consensual Romantic/Sexual Relationships, Discrimination, Harassment, and Title IX Sexual Harassment.

metadata.subsection_title: 2.6 Personnel Files, Transfers, and Promotions

document:
[SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT > 2.6 Personnel Files, Transfers, and Promotions > Personnel Files]

### Personnel Files
HR maintains confidential personnel files. Staff members may submit a written request to HR to review their own personnel file (access frequency may be limited to prevent abuse).

metadata.subsection_title: 2.6 Personnel Files, Transfers, and Promotions

document:
[SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT > 2.6 Personnel Files, Transfers, and Promotions > Transfer and Promotion Eligibility]

### Transfer and Promotion Eligibility
* **12-Month Service Requirement:** Staff members must complete **12 months in their current position** before applying for transfer/promotion to another unit, unless a written waiver is agreed upon by both supervisors and HR.  
* **Performance Requirement:** Staff members who received a "corrective action" rating on their last review or received disciplinary action in the preceding **6 months** are **ineligible** for transfer or promotion.

metadata.subsection_title: 2.7 Transfer Selection Process and Notice Periods

document:
[SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT > 2.7 Transfer Selection Process and Notice Periods > Selection and Salary History Ban]

### Selection and Salary History Ban
* **Salary History Ban:** Northwestern does not inquire about a candidate's salary or benefit history.  
* **References:** Internal/external reference checks are mandatory. Internal checks must include the current supervisor.  
* **Notice Periods for Internal Transfers:** Exempt staff must provide at least **4** weeks working **notice**; Non-exempt staff must provide at least **2 weeks working notice**.  
* **Leave Retention:** Transferring staff retain their accumulated vacation, personal floating holiday, and sick time balances.

metadata.subsection_title: 2.8 Reinstatement, Rehire, and Performance Reviews

document:
[SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT > 2.8 Reinstatement, Rehire, and Performance Reviews > Reinstatement vs. Rehire]

### Reinstatement vs. Rehire
* **Reinstatement (Within 6 Months):** Staff returning to a regular position within 6 months retain prior service credit and benefits status. Benefits re-enrollment period is 30 days.  
* **Rehire (After 6 Months):** Treated as new employees with no prior service credit for paid time accrual. Requires a minimum **31-day break in service**.

metadata.subsection_title: 2.8 Reinstatement, Rehire, and Performance Reviews

document:
[SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT > 2.8 Reinstatement, Rehire, and Performance Reviews > Performance Excellence Framework]

### Performance Excellence Framework
Annual performance reviews are conducted online via **myHR Learn** (learn.northwestern.edu).

* Facilitates goal alignment, continuous feedback, and merit pay decisions.  
* Employees who disagree with their review may attach a **rebuttal letter** to their personnel file or myHR Learn record.

metadata.subsection_title: 2.9 Talent Development, Recognition, and Corrective Action

document:
[SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT > 2.9 Talent Development, Recognition, and Corrective Action > Talent Development & Recognition]

### Talent Development & Recognition
Provides professional, leadership, and organizational development programs (hr.northwestern.edu/talent-development). Features formal and informal recognition for employee contributions.

metadata.subsection_title: 2.9 Talent Development, Recognition, and Corrective Action

document:
[SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT > 2.9 Talent Development, Recognition, and Corrective Action > Corrective Action Process]

### Corrective Action Process
Evaluates work performance, dependability, conduct, and policy compliance.

* **Performance Management:** Communicative (coaching, expectation setting, performance improvement plans).  
* **Corrective/Disciplinary Action:** Disciplinary (written warnings, unpaid suspensions, termination).  
* Eligibility **Impact:** Employees receiving corrective action within the last 6 months cannot transfer or receive a promotion.

metadata.subsection_title: 2.10 Resolving Workplace Issues and Non-Retaliation Policy

document:
[SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT > 2.10 Resolving Workplace Issues and Non-Retaliation Policy > Resolving Workplace Issues]

### Resolving Workplace Issues
Staff can resolve concerns through discussions with supervisors, HR Business Partners (HRBPs), or the Office of Civil Rights and Title IX Compliance (ocr@northwestern.edu). Time spent in HR meetings during work hours is paid.

metadata.subsection_title: 2.10 Resolving Workplace Issues and Non-Retaliation Policy

document:
[SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT > 2.10 Resolving Workplace Issues and Non-Retaliation Policy > Non-Retaliation Policy]

### Non-Retaliation Policy
Northwestern strictly prohibits retaliation against any community member who reports, inquires in good faith, or participates in an investigation regarding wrongful or unlawful activity. Retaliation includes salary reduction, negative evaluations, termination, or creating a hostile environment.

metadata.subsection_title: 2.11 Reporting Misconduct and Resignation Procedures

document:
[SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT > 2.11 Reporting Misconduct and Resignation Procedures > Misconduct Reporting Channels]

### Misconduct Reporting Channels
Employees are obligated to report noncompliance. Options include supervisors, HR, University Compliance, or anonymously via **EthicsPoint** (24/7 phone/web hotline: secure.ethicspoint.com or 866-294-3545).

metadata.subsection_title: 2.11 Reporting Misconduct and Resignation Procedures

document:
[SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT > 2.11 Reporting Misconduct and Resignation Procedures > Resignation / Voluntary Separation]

### Resignation / Voluntary Separation
* **Notice Requirement:** Non-exempt staff must give at least **2 weeks written working notice**; Exempt staff must give at least **1 month (4 weeks) working notice**.  
* **Paid Time Off Restriction:** Vacation or personal floating holidays **cannot** be used to extend the final termination date or as the last workday (except upon retirement).

metadata.subsection_title: 2.12 Involuntary Termination and Post-Termination Procedures

document:
[SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT > 2.12 Involuntary Termination and Post-Termination Procedures > Immediate Discharge Offenses]

### Immediate Discharge Offenses
Gross misconduct resulting in immediate discharge includes criminal conviction, record falsification, theft, physical violence/threats, research misconduct, severe policy violations, or job abandonment.

metadata.subsection_title: 2.12 Involuntary Termination and Post-Termination Procedures

document:
[SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT > 2.12 Involuntary Termination and Post-Termination Procedures > Post-Termination & COBRA Benefits]

### Post-Termination & COBRA Benefits
* **COBRA:** Terminated staff can continue health, dental, vision, and FSA coverage by paying required premiums.  
* **Retirement Continuation:** Retirees (age 55+ with required years of continuous service) can continue health/dental coverage.  
* **Return of Property:** Wildcard IDs, keys, access cards, laptops, and equipment must be returned prior to the final day.  
* **Appeals:** Involuntary terminations may be appealed in writing to the Vice President of HR within **10 calendar days**.

metadata.subsection_title: 2.13 Unpaid Interns and Volunteers Criteria

document:
[SECTION 2: EMPLOYMENT > 2.13 Unpaid Interns and Volunteers Criteria > Intern & Volunteer Guidelines (FLSA)]

### Intern & Volunteer Guidelines (FLSA)
* Interns/volunteers must be at least 16 years old; those over 18 require a background check.  
* **Unpaid Intern Criteria (Primary Beneficiary Test):** Must provide educational training, tie to academic coursework, correspond to academic calendar, complement (not displace) paid staff, and have no expectation of compensation or guaranteed job.  
* **Volunteer Criteria:** Allowed for nonprofit educational activities, offered freely without coercion, and not displacing regular employees.

metadata.subsection_title: 3.1 Civility, Respect, and Ethics Standards

document:
[SECTION 3: REQUIREMENTS IN THE WORKPLACE > 3.1 Civility, Respect, and Ethics Standards > Civility and Mutual Respect]

### Civility and Mutual Respect
Northwestern expects respectful interactions. Demeaning, intimidating, bullying, or violent behavior is strictly prohibited. Violators are subject to disciplinary action up to termination. Campus visitors/vendors failing to comply will be removed.

metadata.subsection_title: 3.1 Civility, Respect, and Ethics Standards

document:
[SECTION 3: REQUIREMENTS IN THE WORKPLACE > 3.1 Civility, Respect, and Ethics Standards > Ethics and Conflict of Interest]

### Ethics and Conflict of Interest
* **Standards for Business Conduct:** Establishes acceptable business standards (policies.northwestern.edu).  
* **Conflict of Interest:** Outside activities/financial interests must not interfere with University obligations. Staff must submit **annual conflict disclosures**. Applies to immediate and extended family members.  
* **Gifts & Hospitality:** Gifts or hospitality above a de minimis value from external vendors must **not** be accepted.

metadata.subsection_title: 3.2 Workplace Safety, Violence Prevention, and Behavioral Consultation

document:
[SECTION 3: REQUIREMENTS IN THE WORKPLACE > 3.2 Workplace Safety, Violence Prevention, and Behavioral Consultation > Prevention of Workplace Violence]

### Prevention of Workplace Violence
* **Weapons Ban:** All weapons (including facsimiles and concealed carry) are prohibited on campus, except for sworn police officers.  
* **Crime Blotter:** University Police maintains a daily crime log accessible online 24/7 or at police stations.  
* **Emergency Reporting:** In imminent danger, call **911**. Non-emergencies: Evanston (847-491-3456) or Chicago (312-503-3456).

metadata.subsection_title: 3.2 Workplace Safety, Violence Prevention, and Behavioral Consultation

document:
[SECTION 3: REQUIREMENTS IN THE WORKPLACE > 3.2 Workplace Safety, Violence Prevention, and Behavioral Consultation > Behavioral Consultation Team (BCT)]

### Behavioral Consultation Team (BCT)
Conducts threat assessments and manages cases involving dangerous, disruptive, or threatening behavior to ensure campus safety (policies.northwestern.edu/docs/bct-policy-final.pdf).

metadata.subsection_title: 3.3 Minors Protection, Hazing, and Political Activities

document:
[SECTION 3: REQUIREMENTS IN THE WORKPLACE > 3.3 Minors Protection, Hazing, and Political Activities > Protection of Minors]

### Protection of Minors
All staff interacting with minors are mandated reporters. Suspected child abuse or neglect must be reported **immediately** to the Illinois DCFS hotline (**800-25-ABUSE**) followed by a written report within 48 hours.

metadata.subsection_title: 3.3 Minors Protection, Hazing, and Political Activities

document:
[SECTION 3: REQUIREMENTS IN THE WORKPLACE > 3.3 Minors Protection, Hazing, and Political Activities > Hazing & Political Activities]

### Hazing & Political Activities
* **Hazing:** Illegal under Illinois law. Silent observation of hazing is a policy violation and must be reported.  
* **Political Activities:** Northwestern is tax-exempt and **cannot endorse or support political candidates**. University facilities cannot be used for political campaigns except by recognized student organizations under strict guidelines.

metadata.subsection_title: 3.4 Drug-Free Workplace and Fitness for Duty Evaluation

document:
[SECTION 3: REQUIREMENTS IN THE WORKPLACE > 3.4 Drug-Free Workplace and Fitness for Duty Evaluation > Drug & Cannabis Policy]

### Drug & Cannabis Policy
* Possession, use, or distribution of illegal drugs or alcohol on University property is prohibited.  
* **Cannabis Notice:** While legal under Illinois state law, cannabis **remains illegal under federal law**. Northwestern strictly prohibits cannabis use, possession, or storage on all campuses and events under the federal Drug-Free Schools and Communities Act.

metadata.subsection_title: 3.4 Drug-Free Workplace and Fitness for Duty Evaluation

document:
[SECTION 3: REQUIREMENTS IN THE WORKPLACE > 3.4 Drug-Free Workplace and Fitness for Duty Evaluation > Fitness for Duty Evaluation]

### Fitness for Duty Evaluation
Employees exhibiting observable difficulty performing duties, unusual disruptive behavior, or personal/physical impairment may be referred by HR for a confidential **Fitness for Duty Evaluation** by a licensed healthcare provider at department expense. Noncompliance may lead to termination.

metadata.subsection_title: 3.5 IT Resources, Security, Confidentiality, and Intellectual Property

document:
[SECTION 3: REQUIREMENTS IN THE WORKPLACE > 3.5 IT Resources, Security, Confidentiality, and Intellectual Property > Use of IT & Network Resources]

Northwestern prohibits discrimination and harassment based on race, color, religion, national origin, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, citizenship, veteran status, or genetic information in all educational and employment activities.

metadata.subsection_title: 4.1 Nondiscrimination, Harassment, and Title IX Policies

[SECTION 4: WORKPLACE COMMITMENT > 4.1 Nondiscrimination, Harassment, and Title IX Policies > Title IX & Sexual Misconduct]

Prohibits sex discrimination, sexual harassment, sexual assault, domestic violence, and stalking. Managed by the **Office of Civil Rights and Title IX Compliance** (ocr@northwestern.edu / 847-467-6165).

metadata.subsection_title: 4.2 Workplace Accommodations and Employee Rights

[SECTION 4: WORKPLACE COMMITMENT > 4.2 Workplace Accommodations and Employee Rights > Reasonable Accommodations]

* **Disability Grievances & ADA:** Overseen by the Director of ADA Compliance.  
* **Pregnancy & Lactation:** Accommodations provided under PWFA/Title IX (frequent breaks, seating, lifting limits, time off). Lactation rooms available on campus.

### Benefits Eligibility
Regular staff scheduled to work at least **18.75 hours per week (0.50 FTE)** are benefits-eligible. Deductions are taken from University paychecks.

metadata.subsection_title: 5.3 Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) Leave

document:
[SECTION 5: BENEFITS > 5.3 Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) Leave > FMLA Eligibility & Provisions]

### FMLA Eligibility & Provisions
Grants eligible staff up to **12 work weeks** of job-protected leave in a **rolling 12-month period** for:

1. Birth or placement of a child for adoption/foster care.  
2. Caring for an immediate family member (spouse, partner, child, parent) with a serious health condition.  
3. Employee's own serious health condition.  
* **Eligibility Criteria:** At least **1 year of service** AND at least **1,250 hours worked** in the past continuous 12 months.  
* **Calculation:** Uses a rolling 12-month lookback period measured backward from the date leave is used.  
* **Concurrent Run:** FMLA runs concurrently with Extended Sick Time (EST).

metadata.subsection_title: 5.4 Specialized Leaves (BAPL, VESSA, Military, Medical)
keywords_tr: doğum ve evlat edinme ebeveyn izni

document:
[SECTION 5: BENEFITS > 5.4 Specialized Leaves (BAPL, VESSA, Military, Medical) > Leave Types Overview]

### Leave Types Overview
* **Birth & Adoption Parental Leave (BAPL):** Paid bonding leave for eligible full-time parents after 1 year of service.  
* **VESSA Leave:** Up to 12 weeks leave for victims of domestic/sexual violence or family crime victims.  
* **Military Leave (USERRA):** Up to 2 weeks paid training differential; full reemployment protection for active duty. Military Caregiver Leave provides up to **26 weeks**.  
* **Workers' Compensation Leave:** Managed by Risk Management for job-related injuries.  
* **Medical Leave (ADA/PWFA):** Unpaid accommodation leave when FMLA is exhausted or ineligible.  
* **Unpaid Personal Leave:** Subject to department approval after 12 continuous months of service (vacation/floating holidays must be exhausted first).

### Vacation Accrual Cap & Payout
* **Accrual Cap:** Maximum vacation balance cannot exceed **1.5 times the annual accrual rate**. Excess balance at fiscal year-end is forfeited.  
* **Termination Payout:** Unused approved vacation balance is paid in a lump sum upon separation.

document:
[SECTION 6: PAID TIME AWAY FROM WORK > 6.3 Incidental Sick Time (IST) and Extended Sick Time (EST) > Incidental Sick Time (IST)]

### Incidental Sick Time (IST)
* Refreshed on **September 1** (15 days for full-year staff; prorated for new hires).  
* Covers short-term personal or family illness, preventive medical appointments, or quarantine.  
* Unused IST **does not carry over** and is **not paid out** upon separation.  
* Medical documentation may be required for absences of **3 or more consecutive days**.

metadata.section_title: SECTION 6: PAID TIME AWAY FROM WORK
metadata.subsection_title: 6.3 Incidental Sick Time (IST) and Extended Sick Time (EST)

document:
[SECTION 6: PAID TIME AWAY FROM WORK > 6.3 Incidental Sick Time (IST) and Extended Sick Time (EST) > Extended Sick Time (EST)]

### Extended Sick Time (EST)
* Available after **6 months of continuous benefits-eligible service**.  
* Provides **100% salary protection for up to 6 months** for an approved extended illness/injury after a **7-calendar day elimination period**.  
* Runs concurrently with FMLA. EST does not offer standalone job protection unless paired with FMLA/ADA accommodation.

metadata.subsection_title: 6.4 Other Paid Time Off Programs

document:
[SECTION 6: PAID TIME AWAY FROM WORK > 6.4 Other Paid Time Off Programs]

* **Non-Benefits Eligible Staff Paid Sick Leave:** Non-benefits staff/students earn 1 hour of paid leave and 1 hour of paid sick time per 35 hours worked (max 40 hrs/yr).  
* **School Visitation:** Up to **8 hours per school year** (max 4 hours/day) for school activities.  
* **Voting Time:** Up to **2 hours paid time off** on election day if unable to vote outside work hours (48 hrs advance notice required).  
* **Bereavement Leave:** **10 days total** for immediate family (first **5 days paid**, remaining 5 unpaid/vacation); 1 day paid for extended family.  
* **Jury Duty:** Full regular salary paid while serving on jury duty; employee retains jury duty stipend.

### Career Path Framework & Pay Grades
Jobs are grouped into functional "Job Families" and assigned market-based pay grades. Pay ranges represent labor market value, skills, and experience. Pay rates cannot fall below the minimum of the assigned pay grade.

### Exempt vs. Non-Exempt Compensation
* **Exempt:** Executive, administrative, professional roles. Paid set monthly salary; **not eligible for overtime pay**.  
* **Non-Exempt:** Paid hourly. Must receive **1.5x hourly rate** for all hours worked over **40 in a workweek**.

document:
[SECTION 8: WORK HOURS AND PAYROLL > 8.1 Workday, Attendance, and Schedule Policies > Work Schedules & Attendance]

### Work Schedules & Attendance
* Standard office hours: 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday–Friday (37.5 or 40 hours/week minimum for full-time). Workweek runs Sunday 12:00 a.m. to Saturday 11:59 p.m.  
* **Unscheduled Absence:** Must notify supervisor daily.  
* **Job Abandonment:** **3 consecutive days** of unexcused absence without notice constitutes job abandonment and results in termination.  
* **Tardiness & Pattern Absences:** Subject to disciplinary action.

document:

### Overtime & Rest Rules
* **Overtime:** Prior supervisor approval required. Paid at **1.5x rate** over 40 hours/week.  
* **Mandatory Rest Period:** Non-exempt staff must receive at least **24 consecutive hours off** every 7-day period.

### Time Reporting & Compensatory Time
* Non-exempt staff report hours daily/biweekly; exempt staff report paid time off monthly.  
* **Compensatory Time Ban:** Taking time off in lieu of overtime pay (comp time) is **strictly prohibited**.

### Meal and Rest Periods
* **Lunch Periods:** Unpaid (30–60 mins). A 20-minute meal break is mandatory for shifts of 7.5+ hours. Meal periods cannot be skipped to shorten the workday.  
* **Rest Breaks:** Paid 15-minute break per half-day shift (if bound to continuous workstation tasks).

* **Pay Frequency:** Non-exempt paid biweekly (Fridays); Exempt paid monthly (last working day of month).  
* **Direct Deposit:** Standard payment method via northwestern.edu/myhr.

### Permissible Deductions for Exempt Staff
Deductions from exempt monthly salary are allowed ONLY for: full-day personal absences (no leave balance), full-day sickness absences under bona fide leave plans, unpaid disciplinary suspensions, FMLA leave, initial/final partial weeks, or major safety violations. Improper deductions will be reimbursed upon investigation.

HR must be notified at least **60 days in advance** if an employee is approved to work remotely outside Illinois (for tax compliance). International remote work is generally **prohibited**.
